after.name: Question 1
after.problem: Suppose $B$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix and $det(B)=-2.$ What is the value of $det(3B)?$
after.worked_solution:
Multiplying a $n\times n$ matrix by a scalar $k$ is equivalent to multiplying each row by $k,$ and this occurs $n$ times. This leads to the result

$$
\begin{aligned}det(k\cdot B)={k}^{n}\cdot det(B).\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, we have $k=3$ and $n=2.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}det(3B) & ={3}^{2}\cdot det(B) \\  & =9\cdot (-2) \\  & =-18.\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 3
after.problem: Suppose $B$ is a $6\times 6$ matrix and $det(B)=-75.$ The matrix $C$ is obtained from $B$ by applying the elementary row operations ${R}_{2}:=\frac{4}{5}{R}_{2}$ and ${R}_{5}↔{R}_{6}.$ What is the value of $det(C)?$
after.worked_solution:
First, let's figure out what each operation does to the determinant.

- The operation ${R}_{5}↔{R}_{6}$ involves swapping two rows, so it changes the sign of the determinant to the opposite one.

- The operation ${R}_{2}:=\frac{4}{5}{R}_{2}$ involves multiplying a row by $\frac{4}{5},$ so the determinant is multiplied by $\frac{4}{5}$ as well.

Therefore, we have to change the sign of the determinant to the opposite one and multiply by $\frac{4}{5}$ as well. Consequently, we get

$$

Suppose B is a 6×6 matrix and det(B)=−75. The matrix C is obtained from B by applying the elementary row operations R2:=45R2 and R5↔R6. What is the value of det(C)?

a

b
90

60
d
−75

Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, let's figure out what each operation does to the determinant.

  • The operation R5↔R6 involves swapping two rows, so it changes the sign of the determinant to the opposite one.

  • The operation R2:=45R2 involves multiplying a row by 45, so the determinant is multiplied by 45 as well.

Therefore, we have to change the sign of the determinant to the opposite one and multiply by 45 as well. Consequently, we get

det(C)=45⋅(−det(B))=−45det(B)=−45⋅(−75)=60.

This changes the sign of the determinant to the opposite one.
Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}det(Y) & =-det(X) \\  & =-(-60) \\  & =60.\end{aligned}
$$
